g1.label: Revenue growth in the next fiscal year
g1.question: Revenue growth in the next fiscal year, the year after the latest filed fiscal year, as a yearly rate. A high percentile means faster growth than most companies in a similar state.

growth_persistence.label: How long the year-1 growth persists
growth_persistence.unit: fraction of the gap still open
growth_persistence.question: How long the next year's growth persists before it fades to the long-run growth rate. It is stated as the fraction of the gap between next year's growth and long-run growth that is still open five years out. A high percentile means growth persists longer than for most similar companies (a slower fade); a low percentile means it fades quickly.

margin_target.label: Long-run operating margin
margin_target.question: The operating margin (operating income divided by revenue) the company settles at in the long run. A high percentile means a higher long-run margin than most similar companies.

margin_retention.label: How long today's margin gap persists
margin_retention.unit: fraction of the gap still open
margin_retention.question: How long the gap between today's operating margin and the long-run margin persists. It is stated as the fraction of that gap still open five years out. A high percentile means the gap persists longer (today's margin is more durable, or the move to the long-run margin is slow); a low percentile means the margin returns to its long-run level quickly.

ronic.label: Return on invested capital five years on
ronic.question: The after-tax operating profit earned per dollar of invested capital (equity plus debt, less cash) five years from now, as a yearly rate. The company starts from its own recent level and moves toward the typical level of its industry; the same level is the return it earns on the new capital it invests to grow. A high percentile means a higher return on capital than most similar companies: growth is cheap for this company, it needs little extra capital for each dollar of added revenue.

g_terminal.label: Long-run (terminal) revenue growth
g_terminal.question: Not a judgment input and not asked (the long-run growth rate is the lower of the risk-free rate and a long-run growth anchor, one value per date). Kept only so that runs made before this change can be read.

rote_target.label: Long-run return on tangible equity
rote_target.question: The through-the-cycle return on tangible equity (net income divided by tangible common equity) the company earns in the long run. A high percentile means a higher long-run return than most similar companies.

rote_retention.label: How long today's return gap persists
rote_retention.unit: fraction of the gap still open
rote_retention.question: How long the gap between today's return on tangible equity and the long-run return persists. It is stated as the fraction of that gap still open five years out. A high percentile means the gap persists longer; a low percentile means the return returns to its long-run level quickly.
